studies.label: In-person pilot of the two-player AUT (GPT vs HUM vs CON, within-person)

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 3, Section 3.2 and Figure 1 caption (continued on PDF p. 4)
counts_source.quote: Each participant (N = 62) runs three randomized 4-minute co-creation sessions—once

arms.name: GPT
arms.description: Each participant completes a live co-ideation chat with a GPT-4 partner and then curates the best creative uses. AI turns are restricted to a single-sentence idea, with server-enforced turn-taking; partner identity is disclosed (PDF pp. 2-3, Sections 3.1-3.2). The randomized count is the within-person cohort, not a separate group.

arms.name: HUM
arms.description: Each participant completes a shared co-ideation chat with another participant, using the same interface and matched task instructions, and then curates the best creative uses. Human turn-taking occurs naturally (PDF pp. 2-3, Sections 3.1-3.2). The randomized count is the same within-person cohort.

arms.name: CON (pooled)
arms.description: Each participant completes a non-interactive session with a pre-rated seed set and then curates uses. This arm pools highly creative human, uncreative human, and GPT-4-only seed sets (PDF p. 3, Section 3.2). The other_aid code follows the reconciled form because the schema has no mixed code; some participants receive AI-generated ideas, so this is not an AI-free control.

arms.name: CON gpt_con
arms.description: CON seed sub-arm showing GPT-4-only ideas, without a live partner. Seed-set assignment is between participants and is not stated to be random (PDF p. 3, Section 3.2 and Figure 1; PDF p. 6, Section 4.3).

arms.name: CON high_con
arms.description: CON seed sub-arm showing highly creative human ideas drawn from Stevenson et al. and selected by agreement between independent researchers. Seed-set assignment is not stated to be random (PDF p. 3, Section 3.2 and Figure 1; PDF p. 6, Section 4.3).

arms.name: CON low_con
arms.description: CON seed sub-arm showing uncreative human ideas drawn from Stevenson et al. and selected by agreement between independent researchers. Seed-set assignment is not stated to be random (PDF p. 3, Section 3.2 and Figure 1; PDF p. 6, Section 4.3).

studies.task: Generate unusual uses for counterbalanced everyday objects (book, fork, tin can) in co-ideation chats or following non-interactive seed exposure, then curate the best uses in a separate survey tab (PDF p. 3, Section 3.2).

ai_tool.name: gpt-4 via OpenAI chat-completions API
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 3, Section 3.1, AI configuration; the model release year is not stated

preregistration.where: No preregistration is reported. PDF p. 4, Section 4, calls the estimates exploratory; PDF p. 7, Section 7, describes the platform as a pre-registerable testbed.

estimates.outcome: Crowd-rated originality of Alternate Uses Test ideas, GPT-4 partner versus human partner
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Originality is defined as how unlikely others would be to generate the idea. Section 3.4 describes independent ratings on a 5-point Likert scale by 226 crowdsourced workers, with median 6 ratings per idea (range 5–12), for a dataset of 1,923 distinct ideas across conditions. The dataset-wide idea count is not the number of rating observations in this contrast. The rated pool may contain both chat contributions and curated ideas.

regression.model: Linear mixed-effects model of originality ratings with fixed effects of partner type, non-interactive assignment, and their interaction; random intercepts for subject, item-within-subject, and rater. The reported coefficient is GPT minus HUM. No outcome standardization or robust-SE procedure is stated.

sources.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 4.1, Baseline Originality Across Partner Types

sources.quote: The dataset contains 1,923 distinct ideas rated by 226 crowdsourced workers (median 6 ratings per idea, range 5–12, with ~3% of ideas double-rated for reliability checks). Each idea received independent originality ratings on a 5-point Likert scale.

sources.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 4, Analysis and Results
sources.quote: We fit a Linear Mixed-effects Model (LMM) with fixed effects of Partner type, non- interactive assignment, and their interaction, plus random intercepts for subject, item-within-subject, and rater.

sources.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 4.1, TOST and Bayesian re-estimation
sources.quote: |β| ≤ 0.33, and a Bayesian re-estimation with a weakly informative Normal(0, 1) prior yielded substantial evidence in favor of the null (BF₀₁ = 10.95; posterior median +0.06, 95% credible interval [−0.06, +0.20]).

estimates.notes: The frequentist LMM coefficient is the extracted main result, in the original rating units; the paper reports no standardized main effect. No first-round-only GPT-versus-HUM estimate, full-sample arm means, participant-level SDs, exact analyzed participant counts, or rating-observation count is printed. The sample size in the study record is the randomized cohort and is not substituted for the missing model counts. Participant random intercepts support se_basis=participant under the codebook, although HUM dyad formation and any dyad dependence remain unspecified. The rater random-effect SD is not an arm outcome SD and is not used as a standardizer. Supplemental analyses of this same contrast are retained here rather than counted as additional estimates: the TOST statement gives |β| ≤ 0.33; Bayesian re-estimation uses Normal(0, 1), BF₀₁ = 10.95, posterior median +0.06, and 95% credible interval [−0.06, +0.20]. These Bayesian quantities are not entered as the frequentist confidence interval or a standardized paper effect. The paper does not explain the difference in sign. Figure 3 reports only BAS Drive subgroup means and graphically drawn CIs; no values are read from bar heights or interval endpoints.

not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 6, Figure 3, splits participants by BAS Drive. These are subgroup contrasts, not eligible full-sample estimates. The means are not recombined, and their plotted confidence intervals are not read off the figure.

not_extracted.what: S1-O3: CON-session originality, CON gpt_con versus CON low_con
not_extracted.reason: Only the within-person session order is stated to be randomized. The between-person seed-set assignment is not stated to be random (PDF p. 3, Section 3.2 and Figure 1; PDF p. 6, Section 4.3). It is also unclear whether the manipulation check rates seed texts or participant-produced ideas (PDF p. 4, Sections 3.4 and 4.1). Not extracted as a randomized human-assistance contrast.

not_extracted.what: S1-O3: CON-session originality, CON gpt_con versus CON high_con
not_extracted.reason: Only the within-person session order is stated to be randomized. The between-person seed-set assignment is not stated to be random (PDF p. 3, Section 3.2 and Figure 1; PDF p. 6, Section 4.3). It is also unclear whether the manipulation check rates seed texts or participant-produced ideas (PDF p. 4, Sections 3.4 and 4.1). Not extracted as a randomized human-assistance contrast.

not_extracted.what: S1-O4: Later originality by first-session CON seed set, including CON gpt_con versus CON high_con and the omnibus seed-set test
not_extracted.reason: The seed-set assignment is not stated to be random. This analysis is restricted to participants whose first session was CON and pools later HUM and GPT sessions (PDF p. 6, Section 4.3). It therefore does not provide a full-sample randomized AI contrast or a separate outcome produced after AI removal.

not_extracted.what: Trait predictors of originality and within-subject originality range, including RMET, BIS/BAS, and random-forest variable importance
not_extracted.reason: PDF pp. 4-5, Sections 3.3 and 4.2 and Figure 2, analyze measured participant traits, their associations, and their interactions. These are not randomized AI-versus-comparator estimates. Within-person variation is not diversity across people.

not_extracted.what: Partner perceptions and originality associations: outsourcing, responsiveness, competence, influence, and effect
not_extracted.reason: Perception items are self-reports, not creativity scored on produced output; their reported associations with originality are non-randomized correlational or moderation analyses (PDF p. 3, Section 3.2; PDF p. 4, Figure 1 text alternative; PDF p. 5, Section 4.2).

not_extracted.what: Utility of Alternate Uses Test ideas
not_extracted.reason: Defined as practical usefulness, but PDF p. 4, Section 3.4, states: "We report originality here; utility results are available on request." No result is printed.

not_extracted.what: Solo Alternate Uses Test before or after the co-creation sessions
not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 3, Section 3.2, describes the solo task as a baseline or practice control. The paper prints no solo-AUT outcome contrast and does not state that assignment to before versus after was randomized.

open_items: The mixed model does not print analyzed participant counts by arm or in total, or its number of rating observations. Figure 3 subgroup counts differ across partner conditions; they are not summed or substituted for model counts. Study and arm n_analyzed and estimate people counts remain null.

No full-sample GPT and HUM means or participant-level outcome SDs are printed. The reported rater random-effect variance is not an eligible standardizer. A standardized effect cannot be transcribed from the main result.
No first-round-only GPT-versus-HUM result is printed; the retained contrast uses all within-person conditions and may be affected by order or carryover.

The rated pool is ambiguous: the Figure 1 caption on PDF p. 4 says curated ideas are rated, while the image on PDF p. 3 describes generated chat plus curated ideas. It is unclear whether GPT-written chat turns are included in the scored outcome.

The procedure for randomizing order and forming HUM dyads is unspecified. The paper gives subject, item-within-subject, and rater random intercepts but no dyad term or dyad-adjusted uncertainty (PDF pp. 3-4, Sections 3.2 and 4).

Dataset counts disagree: PDF p. 2, Section 1.1, and Figure 1 report 1,928 ideas, whereas PDF p. 4, Section 3.4, and PDF p. 7, Section 7, report 1,923. Section 3.4 reports 226 raters, whereas Figure 1 reports 225. These are not participant counts or a known rating-observation count.
The Bayesian posterior and frequentist main estimate differ in sign and interval width without explanation (PDF p. 4, Section 4.1). The Bayesian summary is preserved in estimate notes.

CON seed-set assignment is not stated to be random, exact seed-sub-arm participant counts are not printed, and it is unclear whether the manipulation check scores seeds or participant output. The subsequent-session seed analysis also pools output produced with and without an AI partner (PDF pp. 3-4 and 6).
Utility results are available only on request (PDF p. 4, Section 3.4); no supplementary appendix is included or referenced in the saved document.
The model release year is not stated in the paper, so ai_tool.year remains null.
The local citation record identifies a later ACM proceedings version; body-text differences from the saved arXiv manuscript are unconfirmed.
notes: Extraction A checked the entire markdown conversion and all PDF pages, including the references; there is no appendix. All cited PDF pages were independently text-extracted with pymupdf, and Figures 1 and 3 were inspected from embedded images without creating files. PDF and printed page numbers agree wherever printed. Only the full-sample randomized-order GPT-versus-HUM contrast is extracted. The cohort count and each main-arm n_randomized refer to the same participants, not separate groups; exact analysis counts are left unknown. Country is inferred from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign institution named on PDF p. 3. The AI role is other because the model is a constrained turn-taking co-ideation partner; the CON gpt_con sub-arm instead supplies fixed AI ideas. No diversity outcome or qualifying after-AI contrast is reported. The screening form identifies no shared participant sample; reusing published seed ideas does not imply participant overlap. No effect, SD, SE, interval, arm mean, or participant count has been derived.
